title: Saving a new part number renames the part and its library entry
custom_preconds:
1. You are editing an existing inventory part via the Edit Inventory Part dialog, with "Part Library & Inventory - Create & Edit".
  2. The part has history and sits on at least one work order / invoice / purchase order line.
custom_steps:
1. Edit the number, leave the inline field open, and press Save; confirm the typed number is applied first.
  2. Confirm the part keeps its identity, history and every line that uses it, and its own Part Library entry is renamed (no new entry created).
  3. Save again with the number unchanged and confirm nothing about the number or the entry changes.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Save sends the part number with the rest of the part (if the inline field is still open it is applied first, not dropped); saving a new number renames the part in place - it keeps its identity, history and every work order, invoice and purchase order line, and its own Part Library entry is renamed with it (no new entry created).
  • Saving with the number unchanged changes nothing about the number or the Part Library entry.

Source - where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; "Parts Lifecycle Update" PRD (Confluence 829227015, IN REVIEW 2026-09-09), Story 13 (Edit the part number of an existing part); design canvas Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026 against an IN-REVIEW spec; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S13-R8: “Save sends the part number with the rest of the part. If the field is still open when the user presses Save, the typed number is applied first rather than dropped.”
  • S13-R9: “Saving a new number renames the part in place. The part keeps its identity, its history, and every work order, invoice and purchase order line that uses it. The part's own Part Library entry is renamed with it. No new Part Library entry is created.”
  • S13-R10: “Saving with the number unchanged changes nothing about the number or the Part Library entry.”
